fire: Italian future forms: parlerò, parlerai, parlerà, parleremo, parlerete, parleranno.
Synonyms: reprove, rebuke, upbraid, chide, admonish, reprimand, castigate.
Use the present perfect (have finished) when no time is stated.
Related words: obfuscate, befuddle, perplex, confound, bewilder, nonplus.
In Japanese, the ending -ました marks the polite past tense.
Note the conditional form (would travel) after an if-clause in the past.
quiet: We spoke Italian with our hosts every evening during the trip.

The instructions confused everyone, and nobody knew what to do.
My cousin speaks Portuguese at home with his grandparents.
In Japan, we ate dinner quietly with our host family.
